cats.name: Meredith Grey
cats.story: Meredith Grey is Taylor Swift's Scottish Fold, adopted in late 2011 and named after the Grey's Anatomy lead. She appeared in Swift's Diet Coke and Keds ads and is famous for her aloof, 'sassy' posture. People reported her rare 2025 appearance after Swift bought back her masters.
cats.look: A silver classic tabby-and-white Scottish Fold female with tightly folded ears flat on a round head, a short dense plush coat and a compact cobby body. Bold black swirls cover her crown, with dark stripes between the ears, plus her ears, back, flanks, hips and ringed tail; dark mascara lines run from her big round pale yellow-green eyes. Pure white covers her lower face between and below the eyes, chin, throat, chest, belly and all four legs, and her pink nose has small grey freckles. Her signature is an aloof, half-lidded 'sassy' upright stare.

cats.name: Larry
cats.story: Larry, a brown-and-white tabby from Battersea, has been Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office at 10 Downing Street since February 2011, outlasting several Prime Ministers; CBS reported him awaiting his seventh PM in 2026.

cats.story: Astrophotographer Andrew McCarthy adopted Gregory from an animal shelter in Sep 2024. His post said he took home "the cat with the saddest eyes at the shelter" (20.6M views). A day later he posted: "Sad eyes are gone." On the first anniversary McCarthy wrote that Gregory had been the oldest cat and the longest resident, and is now "a sassy, talkative friend who sits with me while I take photos of space." He photographed Gregory against his space images for the Cosmic Gregory 2026 calendar: basking under the Sun, toying with Saturn and 'representing the solar system' (PetaPixel). He shared the proceeds with the shelter, and on 5 Nov 2025 he donated $10k to Gregory's former shelter. On 5 Sep 2026 he announced that the Cosmic Gregory calendar returns for 2027, with Gregory meeting 'other life forms': fans' cats.
cats.look: A fluffy long-haired orange (ginger) tabby male with a thick cream-white ruff and bib. Darker ginger tabby stripes run across his forehead and cheeks. His muzzle and chin are cream-white and his nose is pink. His amber-gold eyes looked droopy and sad in the shelter carrier photo. His ears are tufted with long pale furnishings, and he has long white whiskers, a plumed tail and a sturdy, heavily furred build. Later photos show a dark collar. PetaPixel (Oct 2025) quotes the vet's estimate that he is 4-5 years old.

In her 18th-birthday photo she is mid-yowl with her mouth wide open and fangs showing, which fits her handle 'myleftfang'. No collar or accessories.

cats.name: Rolf
cats.owner: Helen Bevan, Robb Corrigan and family (live near the University of Warwick campus)
cats.story: Rolf is the University of Warwick's campus cat; Wikipedia's Warwick article says the university 'has a campus cat named Rolf'. He lives with his family (Helen Bevan, Robb Corrigan and family) near campus and calls himself an 'Ambassacat for student health & wellbeing', with #RelaxWithRolf on Fridays. His X account was set up to track his movements across campus and tell students where to find him for a quick meet-up (The Boar). On 7 March 2021 hackers took over the account and replaced his daily updates with posts including a protest about bitcoin. The #CatsOfTwitter community let fans know he was safe, and Twitter support returned the account that Sunday night. Students have called for him to get an honorary degree. His daily 'Rolf report' still runs: posing with his staff ID card for the Exam Team, or being carried round the uni by his 'American Human' with all four paws dangling.

cats.story: Think Think (蔡想想) is the grey tabby of Tsai Ing-wen, former President of Taiwan. cats.name: Sockington
cats.story: Sockington was a grey-and-white shorthair found as a stray outside a Boston subway station in 2004. He lived with archivist Jason Scott in Waltham, Massachusetts. From late 2007 Scott tweeted as him in a breathless cat voice full of shouted capitals. In February 2009 Twitter put @sockington on its recommended list for new users. By May he had half a million followers and The Independent called him 'Twitter's latest megastar'. He passed 1 million in August 2009 and 1.5 million by May 2010, then the most-followed non-human on Twitter. His housemates Pennycat and Tweetie, his 'Sockelganger', tweeted too. He died on 18 July 2022 after 18 years with Scott, who wrote that 'he saw something really shiny in the clouds and decided to chase after it'. Two days later the account posted: 'update I CAUGHT THE RED DOT'.
cats.look: A grey-and-white domestic shorthair: solid slate-grey head, ears, back, legs and tail. White patch on the other cheek too, grey nose leather, white chin, throat and chest. Round amber/yellow-green eyes, upright grey ears, long white whiskers, medium, slightly chunky build. No accessories. His T-shirt (Scott's farewell photo) has his face in a cream-and-gold sunburst medallion under a 'SOCKINGTON' ribbon banner.

cats.name: Mr. B
cats.story: BeeJay, "Mr. B" for short, was a 26-pound, 2-year-old cat at the Morris Animal Refuge in Philadelphia. On 22 August 2019 the shelter posted two photos of a staff member holding him up: "OMG, big boi Mr. B is a CHONK. He's a chonk of a chonk. He redefines the term. Can you guess how much he weighs?" The post now has 35,634 likes and 9,567 reposts; Know Your Meme says it drew more than 40,000 likes and 12,000 retweets in its first 24 hours. CBS Philadelphia reported that the flood of interest crashed the refuge's website that night. The next day, Know Your Meme says, Fox 29 brought him into its studio, where he escaped and hid behind a couch. CBS reported he was described as "a big cat with a big heart", and the shelter called him a "jumbo-sized package of fluff & love".

cats.name: Taters
cats.owner: A NASA JPL employee (unnamed); made public by NASA / NASA JPL
cats.story: Taters is an orange tabby, the pet of a NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory employee, and the star of the first ultra-high-definition video streamed by laser from deep space. The 15-second clip of him chasing a red laser-pointer dot across a sofa was loaded onto the Psyche spacecraft before its October 2023 launch. On 11 December 2023 Psyche's flight laser transceiver beamed it from nearly 19 million miles away, about 80 times the Earth-lunar distance, at 267 Mbps, and it reached Earth in 101 seconds via the Hale Telescope at Palomar. On-screen graphics show his heart rate, colour and breed ("TATERS THE CAT", "ORANGE TABBY"). NASA's X post of the video has 1.97M views, and in April 2025 NASA JPL said Taters and the video were nominated for a Webby Award.
cats.look: A real cat: a ginger tabby-and-white shorthair, solid and slightly chunky. Warm orange coat, soft darker-orange tabby stripes on head, back and flanks, faint forehead 'M' stripes and a long striped, plume-like tail. White muzzle, chin, throat, chest and front legs/paws, running up the face sides. Pink nose, upright pink-lined ears, long white whiskers. Pale amber-green eyes with blue-teal video reflections. Filmed on a dark navy-grey sofa under a sci-fi HUD: mirrored 'THIS IS A TEST' banner, target rings, BPM readout, 'SUBJECT:: TATERS THE CAT / SPECIES:: ORANGE TABBY / LIFE:: 5/9'.

cats.story: Endou Heizou (遠藤平蔵) is the Night-Patrol Cat of Kaoru Fukaya's eight-panel manga Yomawari Neko. He is a grey stray who wears a cat-food can on his head and a hanten jacket. He usually carries the tiger-striped kitten Juurou (重郎). Fukaya posted the first strip to Twitter on 22 October 2015, and retweets by Saho Yamamoto and Shigesato Itoi spread it. His name comes from the surname of a couple Fukaya knows and their cat's name. The series won the 21st Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize (Short Story Award) and became an NHK anime in March 2023, with Takayuki Yamada as Heizou. It has passed 700,000 copies, and volume 12 came out from Kodansha on 22 May 2026.
